bf096f7f980c: MultiDatePick for developers: where configs live (Custom Metadata), Screen Flow outputs, Apex-defined types for loops, user-mode security and sandbox to production.
766da0fc25b7: Do I need to write Apex to use MultiDatePick?
d5247aa0e78c: No. The components load and save records themselves, and flows that save on their own use the packaged Parse Date Entries from JSON action instead of custom Apex.
3a953879bc45: Yes. Each config is a Custom Metadata record (Config__mdt, plus Config_Extension__mdt for newer settings), so it deploys like any other metadata.
f48e4003256f: Does MultiDatePick add objects for my data?
d94bde612031: No. It saves to the objects you choose, so your records, automation and reports stay where they are.
0e6510882db6: How does it handle time zones and languages?
e2ed7a571368: Dates and times follow each user's Salesforce time zone and locale, and the interface is translated into nine languages.

f6f4d13d78ee: MultiDatePick is built so admins never need a developer. This page is for the times a developer or architect is involved anyway: reviewing the package, building flows around it, or moving its setup through sandboxes.

b3759b238c0f: Every saved setup is a <t1>Custom Metadata</t1> record: <t2>Config__mdt</t2> holds the settings, and <t3>Config_Extension__mdt</t3> holds newer ones as JSON in <t4>Settings__c</t4>. A placement on a page or a flow screen names its config in <t5>Config Name</t5>; any property you also set on the placement overrides the config's text and number values.
9c54e314a07e: <t1>Deployable:</t1> configs are metadata, so they move with change sets, the Salesforce CLI or your CI/CD pipeline like any other metadata.
8c102835aa19: <t1>Portable:</t1> the wizard exports a config as JSON and imports it into another org, mapping any object or field that is missing there.
de32b9347f8f: <t1>Reviewable:</t1> one record per setup, readable in Setup, so a change shows up in a diff.
f85fd223b06e: The calendar reads and writes your own objects. There is no MultiDatePick data model to sync, no external service and no callout: picks become ordinary records on the object you choose, with the fields you map (date, end date, start and end time, status, name, resource). Triggers, flows, validation rules and reports on those objects keep working as usual.

7f7d77ab6ddc: Each picked date as <t1>YYYY-MM-DD</t1>. Loop it to create one record per date.
db0d9041a059: Picked ranges, each with a start and end date. Always filled.
fd632423abea: Dates & Times component: each date with its start and end time.
a2529a2a3a24: Resource Booking component: how many bookings the save created.

79565ea8fb43: Every query that returns data, and every save, runs in <t1>user mode</t1>: object permissions, field-level security and sharing apply to the person using the calendar, including guest users on public sites. ae7850cb6e4c: Nothing leaves the org: no callouts, no external servers, no subprocessors.
